staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable snapshot, so every source location below is anchored to its exact line map.

classification.classification_note: An attacker-controlled top-level serialized `variant` hides a 924-byte tuple child whose exact type string declares 1084 variable-sized string members. The outer `variant` fails normal-form checking, so `g_variant_byteswap()` deep-copies it; when recursive tuple-child extraction checks member 0 against the tuple offset table, `gvs_tuple_get_member_bounds()` reads a reverse offset from before the payload because it omits the later `offset_size * (...) <= value.size` guard.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42519197 (glib): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 2 found by fuzz target fuzz_variant_binary_byteswap [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42519197
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source snapshot
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer's `heap-buffer-overflow` against the staged ARVO checkout `a0dbaeed2ffd92e04d5fcdbee3a7c584b32e5581`, and the trace below is anchored to that exact source snapshot. The 2013-byte witness is a top-level serialized `variant` whose final NUL separator sits at byte offset 924; bytes 925..2012 are the exact definite child type string `(tt` plus 1084 `s` members plus `)`. `gvs_variant_get_child()` therefore materializes a 924-byte tuple child with 1086 members total. In `g_variant_byteswap()`, the outer value's type is `v`, so `g_variant_type_info_query()` reports non-zero alignment, and because `g_variant_is_normal_form(value)` reparses the child and rejects that tuple as non-normal, byteswap takes the `g_variant_deep_copy()` path at `gvariant.c:6132` instead of the fast serialised byteswap path. The outer `variant` deep-copy has exactly one child, so it extracts child 0 and materializes a serialized tuple child carrying the same `data`, `size = 924`, and tuple `type_info`. Recursive deep-copy on that tuple immediately requests member 0. `gvs_tuple_get_child()` computes `offset_size = 2` from `value.size = 924`; member 0 is the fixed first `t`, so its own guard passes and the function then calls `gvs_tuple_get_member_bounds()` for the last tuple member to ensure child 0 stays before the offset table. For that final string member, `GVariantMemberInfo.i + 1 = 1083`, but vulnerable `gvs_tuple_get_member_bounds()` checks only that a previous variable-sized member exists before reading `value.data + value.size - offset_size * (member_info->i + 1)`. With the witness this becomes `value.data + 924 - 2 * 1083 = value.data - 1242`, and `gvs_read_unaligned_le()` performs the saved 2-byte read from that underflowed address, matching the AddressSanitizer stack `gvs_read_unaligned_le -> gvs_tuple_get_member_bounds -> gvs_tuple_get_child`. The staged patch resolves this exact obligation by guarding reverse-offset reads with `offset_size * (...) <= value.size`, adding analogous guards for end-offset reads, and treating impossible member bounds as invalid.

source.description: First project-side parse of the attacker-controlled bytes into vulnerability-relevant state. This scans the outer serialized `variant`, splits it at the final NUL separator, and materializes the embedded 924-byte child payload plus its attacker-chosen tuple type info.
source.value_from: The exact 2013-byte witness in `poc` has its last `\0` at byte offset 924. The bytes after that separator are the exact definite type string `(tt` + 1084 `s` + `)`, so the child payload is the first 924 bytes and the parsed child tuple has 1086 members total.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. `bytes` points 1242 bytes before the start of the tuple payload, and the helper copies a 2-byte framing offset from that underflowed address.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 2` at `glib/gvariant-serialiser.c:598` in `gvs_read_unaligned_le`, with stack `gvs_read_unaligned_le -> gvs_tuple_get_member_bounds -> gvs_tuple_get_child`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. On the last-member lookup used to keep child 0 out of the offset table, the tuple-offset reader checks only whether a previous variable-sized member exists; it does not check whether that referenced reverse-offset entry actually fits within the serialized tuple payload before reading it.
root_cause.note: The staged patch adds the missing `offset_size * (member_info->i + 1) <= value.size` guard here, plus analogous guards for the end-offset reads and an invalid-member fallback, confirming this missing bounds obligation.

tainted_value_origin.description: The final-NUL split and attacker-controlled type string are the source-grounded origin of the later `value.size = 924`, tuple `type_info` with 1086 members, `offset_size = 2`, and `member_info->i + 1 = 1083` values that drive the underflow.

parser_admitted.description: The outer serialized `variant` accepts the trailing bytes as one definite child type string, so both the normal-form check and the later outer-child extraction operate on a real serialized tuple child rather than falling back to the default unit tuple `()`.

evidence_limitations: Reviewer feedback in `trace_feedback.json` identified two concrete defects in the earlier GT: it attributed the byteswap branch to the tuple's `t` members instead of the outer `variant` normal-form decision, and it omitted the outer `variant` child-extraction step before recursive tuple deep-copy. The trace below was rebuilt to address both.

The saved AddressSanitizer stack begins at the later deep-copy path, so the step-2 non-normal result is source-grounded inference from the staged `g_variant_is_normal_form()` / `g_variant_serialised_is_normal()` implementation plus the observed branch to `g_variant_deep_copy()` at `gvariant.c:6132`.

Runtime disambiguation remained disabled in `run_flags.json`, so no instrumentation was permitted; the trace is grounded only in the staged vulnerable source, the saved PoC bytes, the staged patch, and the saved AddressSanitizer report.

fine_trace.note: Source. When the outer serialized `variant` is first checked for normal form, this backward scan finds the final NUL at byte offset 924, parses the trailing bytes as the exact definite tuple type `(tt` + 1084 `s` + `)`, and materializes child 0 as a serialized tuple with `child.size = 924`, `child.data = value.data`, and tuple `type_info` for 1086 members.

Because the harness created the outer value with `trusted = FALSE`, this serialized-path check executes instead of returning immediately at line 1340. For type `v`, `g_variant_serialised_is_normal()` dispatches to `gvs_variant_is_normal()`, which reparses child 0 from step 1 and rejects that tuple as non-normal: the 924-byte payload cannot contain the 1083 reverse offset entries implied by 1084 variable-sized `s` members. The call therefore leaves `STATE_TRUSTED` unset and returns false to `g_variant_byteswap()`.

For the outer value's type `v`, `g_variant_type_info_query()` returns non-zero alignment (7, meaning 8-byte alignment). Because step 2 made `g_variant_is_normal_form (value)` false, the fast branch at line 6108 does not take and line 6132 selects `g_variant_deep_copy (value, TRUE)`.

On the outer `variant`, `g_variant_n_children (value)` dispatches to `gvs_variant_n_children()` and yields `n_children = 1`, so deep copy enters its only loop iteration with `i = 0` and requests child 0.

Outer-child extraction reparses the same bytes through `g_variant_serialised_get_child()`, which dispatches back to `gvs_variant_get_child()`, and materializes a new serialized `GVariant` for child 0. That child carries the tuple state's `data = value.data`, `size = 924`, and tuple `type_info`, which is the state the recursive deep-copy uses next.

The recursive `g_variant_deep_copy (child, TRUE)` now runs on the tuple from step 5. For that tuple type, `g_variant_n_children (value)` uses the tuple `type_info` and returns 1086 members, so the first iteration requests tuple member `i = 0`.

For tuple member 0, `offset_size = 2` because `value.size = 924`. Member 0 is the fixed first `t`, so its own guard sees no preceding variable-sized member and does not return. The function then checks that child 0 stays before the offset table by asking `gvs_tuple_get_member_bounds()` for both member 0 and the last tuple member.

For the last tuple member selected in step 7, `member_info` describes the final `s`. The attacker-chosen tuple type contains 1084 variable-sized strings, so the last one has 1083 preceding variable-sized members and therefore `member_info->i + 1 = 1083`.

Root cause. On this last-member lookup, the code checks only `member_info->i + 1` and omits the missing bounds obligation `offset_size * (member_info->i + 1) <= value.size` before reading the reverse offset entry. The patch adds exactly that guard here.

With `value.size = 924`, `offset_size = 2`, and `member_info->i + 1 = 1083`, the unchecked address becomes `value.data + 924 - 2166 = value.data - 1242`, which is 1242 bytes before the start of the tuple payload.
Sink. `gvs_read_unaligned_le()` dereferences the underflowed pointer from step 10 with `size = 2`, producing the saved `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at line 598.

poc.trigger: Feeding the exact 2013-byte witness to `fuzz_variant_binary_byteswap` creates an untrusted top-level serialized `variant` whose child tuple payload is 924 bytes and whose exact trailing type string is `(tt` + 1084 `s` + `)`. `g_variant_byteswap()` rejects that outer value as non-normal, deep-copies into the tuple child, and the first tuple-child fetch underflows the expected 2-byte reverse offset table by 1242 bytes.
